messages.author: c9eec36a3a9e119a
messages.subject: error message when trying to run simple dsm
parts:
Hi All-

I'm sure this is a simple fix, but I can't seem to get past the error message below when trying to run a simple dsm. At this point, I'm simply trying to recreate the dsm example (dolphin data example) with my data to familiarize myself with the code. I'm thinking one of my fields in my observation data isn't numeric and that's causing me problems? I've tried several things and have humbly broken down asking for help. Thanks!

dsm.abundance <- dsm(abundance.est~s(x, y), mcdsLIFESTAGEPRIMARYSUBSTRATE.dist
+               segdata, obsdata, method="REML")


Error in obsdata[, cluster.name]/(fitted.p * availability) : 
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] error message when trying to run simple dsm
parts:
Katy

On first glance, the error message mentions 3 variables: cluster.name, fitted.p and availability.  In most cases, the latter two are computed by the code; leaving the first one (cluster.name) as suspect.  My first debugging question would be "was cluster size read into R correctly?  Did it get read as a factor rather than numerical values?

If that's not the problem, then we'll need to dig deeper.

parts:
Thanks Eric- Converting the size variable to numeric solved that problem, but onto the next error popping up. My final detection function involves a variable at the observation level (Lifestage). This variable is obviously not in my segment data. However, when I try running my dsm, I get the following error:

Error in make.data(response, ddf.obj, segment.data, observation.data,  : 
  Detection function covariates are not in the segment data
  Missing: Lifestage

I've been reading about the differences involving covariates at the observation and segment level for dsm, but any guidance that I seemed to have missed for the detection function step? 

Thanks again-
